dossier.purpose: ntfy is a self-hostable HTTP pub-sub push-notification service with a CLI, a Go client package and a React web app (README.md:28-31). Messages are published with PUT/POST to a topic URL and received via JSON-stream, SSE, raw or WebSocket subscriptions or the mobile/web apps (server/server.go:670-689). For the roles named in the needs (OTLP collector/privacy filter, metrics store, events/logs store, dashboards over those stores, trace/dataset/experiment store, local model server) the checkout contains none of them: no OTLP receiver and no gRPC/protobuf/OpenTelemetry imports in first-party code (OpenTelemetry appears only as indirect Go modules, go.mod:87-95); no telemetry store; no dashboard UI (only an example Grafana JSON for ntfy's own Prometheus /metrics, examples/grafana-dashboard/ntfy-grafana.json); no trace/eval tooling; no model-serving or GPU code. All facts below come from static reading of the v2.28.0 checkout; nothing was built, run or tested.

claims.claim: ntfy ('notify') is 'a simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service'; notifications can be sent 'to your phone or desktop via scripts from any computer, without having to sign up or pay any fees'.
Self-hosting is offered: 'If you'd like to run your own instance of the service, you can easily do so since ntfy is open source.'
A free hosted instance exists at ntfy.sh, plus an open-source Android app (Google Play / F-Droid) and an open-source iOS app (App Store) in separate repositories.
Paid hosted plans ('ntfy Pro') are offered for ntfy.sh for people who don't want to self-host.
Documentation is hosted at ntfy.sh/docs: getting started, Android/iOS, API (publish), install/self-hosting, building.
'The project is dual licensed under the Apache License 2.0 and the GPLv2 License.'
go-sqlite3 (MIT) 'is used to provide the persistent message cache'.
Firebase Admin SDK (Apache 2.0) 'is used to send FCM messages'; webpush-go (MIT) 'is used to send web push notifications'.
Go's text/template (BSD-3-Clause) 'is vendored under template/gotext/ with a small patch adding an execution deadline'; Sprig (MIT) 'is used to add template parsing functions'.
Bundled notification sounds come from Mixkit (Mixkit Free License) and notificationsounds.com (Creative Commons Attribution).
Sponsor banner: 'Special thanks to: Warp, built for coding with multiple AI agents'. This is a sponsorship notice only; Warp is mentioned nowhere else in the repository.

The README is silent on OTLP/OpenTelemetry, telemetry, metrics/Prometheus, dashboards, tracing/evals, Claude Code, Codex, MCP, GPUs and model serving (read in full; a keyword search matches only 'MUI dashboard template' at line 261 and an unrelated substring in a username at line 116).

install.method: Linux release tarball (amd64 shown; armv6/armv7/arm64 variants documented)
install.command:
wget https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/download/v2.28.0/ntfy_2.28.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz
tar zxvf ntfy_2.28.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz
sudo cp -a ntfy_2.28.0_linux_amd64/ntfy /usr/local/bin/ntfy
sudo mkdir /etc/ntfy && sudo cp ntfy_2.28.0_linux_amd64/{client,server}/*.yml /etc/ntfy
sudo ntfy serve

install.method: Debian/Ubuntu apt repository at archive.ntfy.sh (GPG-signed; amd64 shown, armhf/arm64 documented)
install.command:
sudo mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -L -o /etc/apt/keyrings/ntfy.gpg https://archive.ntfy.sh/apt/keyring.gpg
sudo apt install apt-transport-https
echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/ntfy.gpg] https://archive.ntfy.sh/apt stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ntfy.list
sudo apt update
sudo apt install ntfy
sudo systemctl enable ntfy
sudo systemctl start ntfy

install.method: Release .deb or .rpm package (amd64 shown; armv6/armv7/arm64 also documented)
install.command:
wget https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/download/v2.28.0/ntfy_2.28.0_linux_amd64.deb
sudo dpkg -i ntfy_*.deb
sudo systemctl enable ntfy
sudo systemctl start ntfy
# Fedora/RHEL/CentOS:
sudo rpm -ivh https://github.com/binwiederhier/ntfy/releases/download/v2.28.0/ntfy_2.28.0_linux_amd64.rpm
sudo systemctl enable ntfy
sudo systemctl start ntfy

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes: static linux/amd64 binary (tar.gz), deb/rpm packages and a Docker image are release artifacts (.goreleaser.yml:7-15, 68-103, 104-119, 151-158); documented in docs/install.md:12-13, 27-42, 155-265, 357-373.
platforms.wsl2: unknown: no WSL/WSL2 mention in the README or docs (repo-wide search found only unrelated text). A linux/amd64 binary and a native Windows amd64 build exist (docs/install.md:332-355), but WSL2 itself is undocumented.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes, CLI client only: a universal darwin (amd64+arm64) binary built with CGO disabled and the `noserver` tag (.goreleaser.yml:58-67, 137-140). docs/install.md:302-321 say only `ntfy publish`/`ntfy subscribe` are supported on macOS and the server is not supported (it can be built from source for development: Makefile:207-215).
platforms.gpu: no: there is no GPU/CUDA/inference code or documentation; a repo-wide search for gpu|cuda|nvidia|rtx matched only unrelated identifiers.

integrations.cli: Yes. A single `ntfy` binary with `serve`, `publish` (aliases pub/send/trigger; --wait-cmd/--wait-pid publish when a command or PID finishes), `subscribe` (alias sub; prints JSON per message, runs a command per message with NTFY_* env vars, or runs as a service from client.yml via --from-config) and server-side admin commands `user`, `access`, `token`, `tier`, `webpush keys` (cmd/serve.go:125-141, cmd/publish.go:22-88, cmd/subscribe.go:32-83, cmd/user.go:44, cmd/access.go:26, cmd/token.go:21, cmd/tier.go:33, cmd/webpush.go:23; docs/subscribe/cli.md:26-96). The admin commands are excluded from `noserver` (macOS) builds.
integrations.mcp: None found in this repository. The only matches for 'mcp' are links to a third-party 'ntfy-me-mcp' server (github.com/gitmotion/ntfy-me-mcp; docs/integrations.md:182); that external repository was not opened.
integrations.sdk_or_api: HTTP API: publish via PUT/POST /{topic} (also GET /{topic}/publish|send|trigger and JSON publishing), subscribe via GET /{topic}/json, /sse, /raw, /ws with poll and since= replay, update/delete/clear by sequence ID, built-in webhook templates for github, grafana and alertmanager (server/server.go:670-689; server/templates/*.yml; docs/publish.md:2925-2963, 3549; docs/subscribe/api.md:9-237). Also /v1/health, public /v1/stats, /metrics when enabled, and account/admin REST under /v1 (server/server.go:105-136, 563-698). First-party Go client package client/ (Publish/PublishReader/Poll/Subscribe, client/client.go:78-205); no other first-party SDKs, community libraries are only listed (docs/integrations.md:69-88). No OTLP endpoint.
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: None found. A repo-wide search for claude|codex matches only docs/releases.md:359 (a release note saying the PostgreSQL code was written by Cursor and Claude). There are no hooks, plugins, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md or other agent config files.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry, analytics or phone-home code exists in the Go server/CLI or the web app: repo-wide searches find only payments/payments.go:17-21, which sets stripe.EnableTelemetry=false (docs/privacy.md:91); the web app's VersionChecker only polls its own server's /v1/config every 5 minutes (web/src/app/VersionChecker.js:6,48). No OTLP/OpenTelemetry code is in first-party sources (OpenTelemetry modules are only indirect Go dependencies, go.mod:87-95). The server connects out only for features the operator configures: iOS `upstream-base-url` poll-request forwarding, which sends the message ID and the SHA-256 of the topic URL (cmd/serve.go:71-72; server/server.go:1096-1126; docs/config.md:1598-1638), Firebase FCM via `firebase-key-file` (server/server.go:281-294), outgoing SMTP (mail/sender.go:129), Twilio (twilio/client.go:101,140), Stripe (payments), S3 attachments via an `s3://` URL (server/server.go:338-345), Web Push to browser-vendor endpoints (server/server_webpush.go:159) and PostgreSQL via `database-url`. Incoming SMTP and Matrix requests are handled in-process (server/smtp_server.go:196-213; server/server.go:2115-2131). The ntfy CLI defaults to the public hosted service https://ntfy.sh unless `default-host` or a full topic URL is given (client/config.go:11,40; client/client.yml:6). Server defaults: open read-write access for anyone who can reach it (cmd/serve.go:53; docs/config.md:611-613), listens on :80 (server/config.go:19), keeps messages in memory for 12 h (docs/config.md:486-487), and logs topic names and IP addresses (docs/faq.md:25-29). At log-level trace it dumps full request headers (including Authorization) and message bodies without redaction (server/server.go:500-501, 930-931; server/log.go:100-127). Prometheus /metrics and pprof listeners are off unless enabled (cmd/serve.go:113-115; docs/config.md:2226-2269). No account is required for core use; optional external accounts or services are Firebase, Twilio, Stripe, an SMTP relay, S3 and, for hosted use, ntfy.sh. The Android/iOS apps use Firebase Cloud Messaging for the ntfy.sh host (docs/privacy.md:58-67, 105-130); those apps live in separate repositories that were not opened.

languages: Go (server, CLI, client; go.mod 'go 1.25.8'; CI/release toolchain pinned to 1.27.0 in .go-version)
JavaScript/JSX (React + MUI + Vite web app in web/)
Python (only MkDocs documentation build dependencies, requirements.txt)
Shell, Make and YAML (build, packaging, examples)

entry_points.what: Binary `ntfy`: sets version/commit/date via ldflags and runs the urfave/cli app built by cmd.New() (main.go:19-42).
`ntfy serve`: starts the server; dozens of flags, env vars and config-file keys (cmd/serve.go:33-123, 125-141); compiled out by the `noserver` build tag.
`ntfy publish` (aliases pub, send, trigger): CLI publisher with --wait-cmd/--wait-pid, attachments and templates (cmd/publish.go:22-88).
`ntfy subscribe` (alias sub): prints JSON per message, runs a command per message, or runs as a service from client.yml (cmd/subscribe.go:32-83).
server.New / (*Server).Run: HTTP, HTTPS, Unix-socket and SMTP listeners plus optional metrics and pprof listeners; route table handleInternal (server/server.go:178-325, 349-439, 563-698).

Server-side admin commands `ntfy user|access|token|tier` (cmd/user.go:44, cmd/access.go:26, cmd/token.go:21, cmd/tier.go:33) and `ntfy webpush keys` (cmd/webpush.go:23); present only in !noserver builds.
Go client library: Client.Publish/PublishReader/Poll/Subscribe/Unsubscribe (client/client.go:78-205); config in client/config.go.

One-off SQLite to PostgreSQL migration program. Other helper mains (tools/loadtest, tools/loadgen, tools/fbsend, tools/s3cli) are dev tools; GoReleaser builds only the root main.go (.goreleaser.yml:6-67).

code.architecture: One Go module (heckel.io/ntfy/v2) building a single `ntfy` binary: main.go calls cmd/, the urfave/cli layer (serve, publish, subscribe, user, access, token, tier, webpush; YAML/env/flag loading in cmd/config_loader.go). server/ is the HTTP/WebSocket/SMTP server: server.go holds the route table (handleInternal) and publish/subscribe fan-out to in-memory topics (topic.go), visitor.go does per-visitor rate limiting, server_account.go/server_admin.go/server_auth.go handle accounts, admin and auth, server_template.go renders user templates using the vendored template/gotext and util/sprig, and optional integrations live in server_firebase.go, server_webpush.go, server_matrix.go, server_twilio.go, server_payments.go and smtp_server.go (several gated by build tags nofirebase, nowebpush, nopayments, noserver). Storage: message/ (message cache: in-memory by default, SQLite, PostgreSQL or no-op; server/server.go:327-336), user/ (users, ACLs, tokens, tiers; SQLite/PostgreSQL), webpush/ (subscriptions), attachment/ plus s3/ (filesystem or S3 attachments), db/ (pgx pool with read replicas, schema migrations). metrics/ defines 21 Prometheus collectors served at /metrics when enabled; ban/ writes a fail2ban-style ban file; log/ is the structured logger (trace to error, text or JSON); client/ is the Go client used by the CLI. The React web app (web/) and MkDocs docs (docs/) are built and embedded into the binary via `//go:embed site` and `//go:embed docs` (server/server.go:144-152).
code.packaging_and_release: Releases are cut by GoReleaser v2 (.goreleaser.yml:1) through `make release` (Makefile:389-390), triggered by pushing a tag matching v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+ (.github/workflows/release.yaml:3-5, 46-49). `make release` first runs release-checks (docs/install.md and docs/releases.md must mention the tag, clean git tree, Go must equal .go-version; Makefile:395-412) and the full `check` suite (Makefile:389). Artifacts: statically linked Linux binaries in tar.gz for amd64, armv6, armv7 and arm64 (CGO, -extldflags=-static; .goreleaser.yml:7-47, 104-119), Windows amd64 zip (:48-57, 120-128), macOS universal client-only tar.gz (:58-67, 129-140), deb and rpm via nfpm (:68-103), and Docker Hub images binwiederhier/ntfy for amd64/arm64v8/armv7/armv6 with latest, <tag>, v<major> and v<major>.<minor> manifests (:151-206; Dockerfile is `FROM alpine`, no USER). A checksums.txt is generated (:141-142) and printed in CI (Makefile:264-272). No signing, attestation, SBOM or provenance step exists in the release workflow or GoReleaser config (a search for cosign/attest/sbom/signs/gpg found only the NodeSource key in Dockerfile-build:10-11). The documented apt repository archive.ntfy.sh is GPG-signed with a published fingerprint (docs/install.md:158-175) but its publishing pipeline is not in this repository. GoReleaser is installed with @latest (Makefile:245-246); GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs (release.yaml:28-40). v2.28.0 is dated Aug 27, 2026 (docs/releases.md:9, 16).
code.tests_and_ci: Go: standard `testing` plus stretchr/testify (go.mod:15); 76 _test.go files holding 971 top-level Test/Example functions (970 Test + 1 Example; no Benchmark or Fuzz functions), e.g. server/server_test.go 219 and user/manager_test.go 107, spread over server/, user/, message/, s3/, util/ (incl. util/sprig), cmd/, client/, ban/ and others; helper packages test/ and db/test/. PostgreSQL and S3 tests skip unless NTFY_TEST_DATABASE_URL / NTFY_TEST_S3_URL are set (db/test/test.go:19-24; attachment/store_s3_test.go:17-19). Web: vitest, 7 test files in web/src/app (about 90 it/test cases). Workflows in .github/workflows: test.yaml (push to main and PRs, ubuntu-latest only, Postgres 17 service; runs `make docs`, `make web`, `make checkv` = Go tests + prettier/gofmt/go vet/eslint/golint/staticcheck/vendored-template drift check, then `make coverage` = `go test -race -coverprofile`); build.yaml (push to main and PRs; `make build` = web + docs + GoReleaser snapshot builds for all targets); docs.yaml (push to main; builds MkDocs and pushes to binwiederhier/ntfy-docs.github.io); release.yaml (tag push, see above). No workflow calls `make coverage-upload` (Makefile:303-304), so the README codecov badge (README.md:21) is not fed by these workflows. Dependabot runs weekly for npm, gomod and github-actions with a 7-day cooldown (.github/dependabot.yml:1-26). Tests were not executed here.
code.dependencies: go.mod: 21 direct and 69 indirect Go modules (68 in the require blocks plus github.com/pkg/errors at go.mod:28), direct ones at go.mod:10-23 and 31-38 (go-smtp, mimetype, gorilla/websocket, go-sqlite3, olebedev/when, testify, urfave/cli/v2, x/crypto, x/sync, x/term, x/time, google.golang.org/api, yaml.v2, firebase.google.com/go/v4, webpush-go, pgx/v5, bluemonday, prometheus/client_golang, stripe-go/v74, x/sys, x/text); a replace pins go-smtp to v0.17.0 although require says v0.25.0 (go.mod:10,26). tools/loadtest/go.mod is a separate module with 1 dependency (gorilla/websocket). web/package.json: 18 dependencies plus 12 devDependencies, react and react-dom set to 'latest' (lines 26-27), web/package-lock.json present and `npm ci` used (Makefile:154). requirements.txt: 2 unpinned Python packages (mkdocs-material, mkdocs-minify-plugin) used only to build docs. Vendored in-tree: template/gotext (Go stdlib text/template, BSD-3-Clause, patched) and util/sprig (Sprig, MIT).
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md: only the latest version is supported (SECURITY.md:5); vulnerabilities are to be reported privately to security@mail.ntfy.sh (SECURITY.md:9) or via Discord/Matrix (SECURITY.md:11-12). GitHub security advisories are referenced in the changelog (GHSA IDs at docs/releases.md:213, 250) and in template/gotext/README.md:21.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:28 - ntfy is 'a simple HTTP-based pub-sub notification service'
claim_checks.evidence: Publish routes (PUT/POST /{topic}, GET /{topic}/publish|send|trigger) and subscribe routes (GET /{topic}/json|sse|raw|ws) are in the route table at server/server.go:670-689; topic and path regexes at server/server.go:84-95. Static read only.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:29-30 - notifications can be sent from any computer 'without having to sign up or pay any fees'
claim_checks.evidence: The user/auth manager is created only when auth-file or database-url is set (server/server.go:256-280) and auth-default-access defaults to read-write (cmd/serve.go:53; docs/config.md:611-613), so a default server accepts anonymous publish and subscribe, subject to per-visitor limits (burst 60, one request per 5 s; server/config.go:96-97). The CLI defaults to the hosted https://ntfy.sh (client/config.go:11).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:30-31 - 'you can easily [run your own instance] since ntfy is open source'
claim_checks.evidence: `ntfy serve` exists (cmd/serve.go:125-141) and the Linux (static amd64/armv6/armv7/arm64) and Windows release binaries include the server (.goreleaser.yml:7-57). The official macOS binary is built with CGO off and the `noserver` tag (.goreleaser.yml:58-67) and docs/install.md:319-321 say the server is not supported on macOS. The default listen address :80 (server/config.go:19) needs root or CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE (server/ntfy.service:11) unless --listen-http is changed.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:252 - 'dual licensed under the Apache License 2.0 and the GPLv2 License'
claim_checks.evidence: Both full texts are present (LICENSE:1-2 Apache 2.0; LICENSE.GPLv2:1-2 GPL v2), but no source file carries an SPDX identifier or per-file licence header (the only SPDX hits are inside GitHub webhook test fixtures under server/testdata). Metadata is inconsistent: nfpm package licence 'Apache 2.0' (.goreleaser.yml:73), web/index.html:25 'Apache License 2.0', Dockerfile:8 'Apache-2.0, GPL-2.0', CLI banner 'Apache License 2.0 & GPLv2' (main.go:28).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:266 - go-sqlite3 'is used to provide the persistent message cache'
claim_checks.evidence: SQLite is used only when cache-file is set (server/server.go:332-333). The default cache is in-memory for 12 h and lost on restart (server/server.go:335; docs/config.md:486-487), cache-duration 0 disables it (server/server.go:328-329), and PostgreSQL via pgx is an alternative backend (cmd/serve.go:44; server/server.go:330-331; docs/config.md:420-430). The README's third-party list also omits direct dependencies such as pgx, Prometheus client_golang, Stripe, bluemonday and gorilla/websocket (README.md:254-276 vs go.mod:10-37).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:267 - Firebase Admin SDK 'is used to send FCM messages'
claim_checks.evidence: server/server_firebase.go (build tag !nofirebase, line 1) with firebase.google.com/go/v4 (go.mod:31); active only when firebase-key-file is set (cmd/serve.go:43, 325-328; server/server.go:281-294); docs/config.md:1571-1596 call it optional. Release builds do not set the nofirebase tag (.goreleaser.yml:11), so the SDK is compiled in even when unused.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:269, 276 - Go's text/template is vendored under template/gotext/ with a small execution-deadline patch; Sprig 'is used to add template parsing functions'
claim_checks.evidence: template/gotext/README.md:1-11 and 54-64 describe the verbatim stdlib copy plus patches/0001-exec-context.patch, with drift checks in Makefile:333-374; it is used for user-supplied templates (template/gotext/README.md:33-36; server/server_template.go:19). Sprig is a vendored copy at util/sprig/ (util/sprig/LICENSE.txt:1, Masterminds), imported at server/server_template.go:21, not a go.mod module.

claim_checks.claim: docs/install.md:158-175 - the Debian/Ubuntu apt repository at archive.ntfy.sh is GPG-signed (fingerprint 55BA 774A 6F5E E674 31E4 B6B7 CFDB 962D 4F1E C4AF)
claim_checks.evidence: The signed repository is hosted outside this repository; no workflow, script or config here builds, signs or publishes it (a search of .github, Makefile, .goreleaser.yml and scripts/ for gpg/cosign/sign found only the NodeSource key in Dockerfile-build:10-11). GitHub release artifacts get only checksums.txt (.goreleaser.yml:141-142).

claim_checks.claim: docs/config.md:2227 - 'ntfy can expose a /metrics endpoint for Prometheus' (the only monitoring surface; the README is silent on it)
claim_checks.evidence: metrics/metrics.go:14-107 defines and registers 21 Prometheus collectors (messages, Firebase, e-mail, calls, UnifiedPush, Matrix, attachments, visitors, users, subscribers, topics, HTTP requests). The handler is mounted at /metrics or on metrics-listen-http when enabled (server/server.go:415-422, 660) and is off by default (cmd/serve.go:113-114; server/server.yml:466-467). It is a pull endpoint for ntfy's own server metrics; no OTLP export or ingestion exists.

claim_checks.claim: docs/privacy.md:159-161 - when self-hosting, 'No data is shared with ntfy.sh or any third party (unless you configure those integrations)'
claim_checks.evidence: No analytics/telemetry code exists in first-party Go or web sources (only payments/payments.go:17-21 disabling Stripe telemetry). Outbound calls are config-gated: upstream poll forwarding (server/server.go:1096-1126), Firebase (server/server.go:281-294), SMTP (mail/sender.go:129), Twilio (twilio/client.go:101,140), Web Push (server/server_webpush.go:159), S3 (server/server.go:338-345). Incoming SMTP and Matrix requests are handled in-process (server/smtp_server.go:196-213; server/server.go:2115-2131). Caveats: the CLI's default host is ntfy.sh (client/config.go:11) and trace logging dumps headers and bodies (server/server.go:500-501, 930-931). Static read only.

risks: Scope: ntfy is a push-notification pub-sub service, not an observability or inference stack. First-party code has no OTLP receiver or privacy-filter pipeline (route table server/server.go:563-698; no gRPC/protobuf/OpenTelemetry imports, OpenTelemetry only as indirect modules go.mod:87-95), no store for telemetry events/logs/traces/datasets, no dashboard UI beyond an example Grafana JSON for its own Prometheus metrics (examples/grafana-dashboard/ntfy-grafana.json), and no model-serving or GPU code. The only agent-related integration referenced is a third-party MCP server (docs/integrations.md:182) that was not reviewed; no Claude Code or Codex hook/plugin exists in this repo.

Open-by-default exposure: the server listens on :80 on all interfaces (server/config.go:19; docker-compose.yml:13-14) and auth-default-access is read-write, so anyone who can reach the port can publish to and read any topic until auth-file or database-url plus deny-all are configured (cmd/serve.go:53; docs/config.md:611-626); topic names are the only secret (docs/index.md:11-13). The Docker image has no USER directive and runs as root unless -u is passed (Dockerfile:1-16; docs/install.md:386-396).

Wrong-destination default: `ntfy publish` and `ntfy subscribe` use the public hosted https://ntfy.sh unless default-host or a full topic URL is set (client/config.go:11,40; client/client.yml:6), and topics on ntfy.sh are public (docs/publish.md:4910-4912), so an unconfigured CLI would send message text to a third-party service.

Sensitive logging: at log-level trace the server logs every HTTP request in full (all headers including Authorization, plus up to 4 KB of body) and the full message JSON, with no redaction (server/server.go:500-501, 930-931; server/log.go:100-127; no redaction code in log/ or server/log.go). Docs only say debug/trace are 'very verbose' and should be used briefly (docs/config.md:2282-2283). Normal levels log topic names, client IPs and body sizes (docs/faq.md:25-29; model/model.go:55-71).

Release integrity and supply chain: GitHub release artifacts and Docker Hub images come with only a checksums.txt, with no signatures, attestations or SBOM in .goreleaser.yml or release.yaml; GoReleaser is installed with @latest at release time (Makefile:245-246); the Docker base image is the untagged `alpine` (Dockerfile:1). Release binaries compile in the Stripe, Firebase/Google Cloud and Web Push SDKs because no nofirebase/nopayments/nowebpush tags are set (.goreleaser.yml:11), part of 21 direct plus 69 indirect Go modules (go.mod).

Platform limits: the official macOS release is client-only (CGO off, `noserver`; .goreleaser.yml:58-67) and docs state the server is unsupported on macOS (docs/install.md:319-321); building the server from source needs CGO for SQLite (docs/develop.md:14-15); WSL2 is not documented anywhere; CI runs on ubuntu-latest only (.github/workflows/test.yaml:8).

Maintenance and drift: SECURITY.md supports only the latest release (SECURITY.md:5). Releases are frequent (v2.12.0 May 29, 2025 to v2.28.0 Aug 27, 2026; docs/releases.md) and 2026 releases fixed SSRF (v2.22.0), web-app script execution via a crafted SVG preview (v2.23.0), template CPU/memory DoS (v2.26.0, v2.27.0) and unbounded replay cost (v2.28.0) (docs/releases.md:15-28, 41-44, 110-112, 213, 250). The PostgreSQL backend was written by AI tools and reviewed by the maintainer and stayed 'experimental' until v2.27.0 (docs/releases.md:33-36, 356-364). go-smtp is held at v0.17.0 by a replace while require says v0.25.0 (go.mod:10,26); the Go pin (.go-version 1.27.0) differs from go.mod (1.25.8), docs/develop.md:68 (1.25.8) and Dockerfile-build:1 (golang:1.25).

Licensing: README.md:252 says dual licensed under Apache 2.0 and GPLv2 without SPDX identifiers, per-file headers, or wording on whether the licensee may choose either; package metadata names only Apache 2.0 (.goreleaser.yml:73; web/index.html:25) while the Docker label lists both (Dockerfile:8). Vendored stdlib text/template (BSD-3-Clause) and Sprig (MIT) are in-tree (template/gotext/README.md:106-109; util/sprig/LICENSE.txt), and bundled sounds use the Mixkit Free License and CC-BY (README.md:256-257). The 'OR' in this dossier's SPDX expression is an interpretation of 'dual licensed'.

checks.note: docs/privacy.md:161 reads as quoted, and every evidence citation matches. Each outbound path is gated by a setting: payments.go:19 sets stripe.EnableTelemetry=false. forwardPollRequest (server.go:1096-1126) runs only when UpstreamBaseURL != "" (server.go:849), which defaults to "" (cmd/serve.go:71). Firebase needs FirebaseKeyFile (server.go:282). The SMTP sender needs SMTPSenderAddr (server.go:180, 843; mail/sender.go:129). Twilio needs TwilioAccount (server.go:846; twilio/client.go:101, 140). Web Push needs WebPushPublicKey (server.go:220, 852; server_webpush.go:159). S3 needs an s3:// attachment dir (server.go:339). Incoming SMTP is passed to the server's own handler through an httptest recorder (smtp_server.go:196-213), and Matrix requests are rewritten in-process (server.go:2115-2131; server_matrix.go:108-142). The caveats are confirmed: client/config.go:11 DefaultBaseURL is https://ntfy.sh, and trace logging writes out all headers and up to 4 KB of the request body (server/log.go:100-127). A search for telemetry/analytics found nothing else in first-party Go or web code. The embedded docs set font: false (mkdocs.yml:12), so they don't load Google Fonts. The web app's hard-coded ntfy.sh (SubscribeDialog.jsx:34, 95) is only an autocomplete suggestion. VersionChecker polls only its own /v1/config (VersionChecker.js:48).
